patients.label: 52-year-old immunosuppressed man with fatal Acanthamoeba granulomatous amoebic encephalitis

identity_evidence.quote: We present a fatal case of amoebic encephalitis due to Acanthamoeba spp. in an immunosuppressed male.
52-year-old immunosuppressed male presented with fever, impaired consciousness and headache.

attribution_limitations: The five lines after the MRI paragraph form the bullet list of the case report's own "Differential diagnoses" section, so all five are recorded as this patient's differentials (assertion possible). The tumour line says "primary or secondary from previous gastric cancer" without choosing either, and no line states that a differential was excluded.
The source says the patient required intubation but does not state that intubation was carried out.
Prednisolone is described as ongoing at presentation ("was being treated"); no dose, route, indication or later status is stated, and the cause of the immunosuppression is not named in one statement.
Table 1 to Table 4 summarise 29 reviewed cases that include the current case; the tables are not separated by case, so none of their counts or percentages are individual patient values.
The text states "our case report represents a fairly typical history and series of imaging findings"; this is an author conclusion about the case relative to the review, not an individual finding.
Culture, lavage, CSF and imaging results carry no stated dates or order relative to one another; the order of microbiology, brain CT and MRI is not stated.

His history included curatively resected T1N0M0 gastric cancer complicated by post-operative pancytopenia, aplastic anaemia diagnosed on bone marrow biopsy, and bone marrow transplantation leading to graft versus host disease. At presentation he had pancytopenia and was being treated with prednisolone.

claims.text: Chest CT showed a dense right upper lobe mass consolidation with ground-glass opacity. Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus, bronchiolar lavage grew Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and cerebrospinal fluid examination was unremarkable. Serial brain CT 2 days apart showed a rapidly growing low density left parietal mass; non-contrast MRI showed 50 mm left parietal and 33 mm left occipital lesions with haemorrhagic change and restricted diffusion. Differentials were infective encephalitis (primary), tumour, infarction (less likely), post-transplantation lymphoproliferative disease and tumefactive demyelination.
